archetype.name: Pocket Passer (vertical turn)
archetype.definition: A small, rhythm-based passer who barely runs, now asked to drive a pass-heavy offense by attacking 10-plus yards downfield from the pocket.

report.headline: Year four's downfield leap is real; the last three weeks say temper it.
report.take:
For three years Bryce Young was a short-area passer. He averaged 5.46 yards an attempt as a rookie, and in 2024 and 2025 his EPA per play sat around zero, ranking in the 30s. This season he leads the league in passing yards per game at 309.8, ranks 10th of 45 in EPA per dropback at 0.212, and his yards per attempt are up 1.41 from last year. The style has changed with the results. His intended air yards are 9.78, against a 6.9 aDOT last year, and his aggressiveness is up as well. Dave Canales' offense passes 6.2 points over expectation in neutral situations, second-most in the league. Some of the yardage lead is that volume of 40-plus attempts a game, but not all of it.

The production comes almost entirely from throws of 10 or more air yards. On those 75 attempts he has a 0.669 EPA, a +10.2 CPOE and 50.2 EPA in total, which is more than all of his dropbacks added up. Under 10 air yards he is roughly average at 0.072, and screens and other throws behind the line have cost 13.6 points. The middle of the field has been his best area (0.651 EPA), and Tetairoa McMillan, Jalen Coker and John Metchie have each been well above water per target. On this evidence he is a better intermediate and deep thrower than he has ever been, and the offense is built to let him use that.

The headline numbers hide two things. The first is the deep CPOE of +12 on only 26 attempts, which is the kind of figure that drifts back. Hard games have also exposed him. On third down he has a -0.082 EPA with six sacks in 48 plays, and in close fourth quarters his CPOE is -4.1. The second is the trend. Over the last three games his EPA per dropback is 0.137 and his CPOE is -0.6, a 3.9-point drop from the season mark. Week 3 at Cleveland had a 25.6% bad-throw rate and -5.9 EPA. Week 6 at Philadelphia, with left tackle Monroe Freeling out, finished at -8.2 CPOE. The best game of that stretch came against Detroit, now the 32nd-ranked defense. Week 1's big line was also run up while chasing a 59-point opponent.

The likely path is a good starter rather than a top-10 one: a high-volume, above-average EPA passer whose efficiency eases toward the 0.10-0.15 range. The low interception rate and the improved bad-throw rate (down 2.4 points from last year) look like real growth. The 37-touchdown pace does not.

strengths.title: Winning 10-plus yards downfield
strengths.body: His throws of 10 or more air yards carry the whole passing game, with a +10.2 CPOE and a 0.669 EPA. The intermediate zone (0.594 EPA on 49 attempts) is the sturdier part, because that sample is larger and less dependent on a handful of completions than the deep numbers. Expect the deep efficiency to slip, but the willingness to throw there is a real change in profile.

strengths.title: Volume baked into the scheme
strengths.body: Carolina throws far more than situations call for, and he plays every snap of it. That is why he leads the league in yards per game even though his yards per attempt rank 13th. Volume is the most durable part of his line because it comes from scheme rather than from luck.

strengths.title: Avoiding sacks and giveaways
strengths.body: He turns only 16.7% of pressures into sacks, fourth-best among qualifiers, which continues a trend from the last two seasons. His interception rate of 1% ranks 12th, helped by fewer bad throws than last year. The sack avoidance is a career trait. The interception rate is better than his history and will probably rise somewhat.

concerns.title: Efficiency fading over three weeks
concerns.body: The last three games show lower EPA per dropback, a CPOE below zero and a TD rate down 1.6 points. Inaccurate stretches against Cleveland and Philadelphia were balanced only by a Detroit defense that ranks last. This is the clearest signal that the first two weeks overstated his level.

concerns.title: Third down and late leverage
concerns.body: On third down, with an average of 7.9 yards to go, he converts a third of the time with negative EPA and has taken half of his sacks there. In close fourth quarters his accuracy falls below expected. Some of that is long distances created by a mediocre run game, but leverage downs have been a weak spot for his whole career.

concerns.title: Quick game producing nothing
concerns.body: The throws behind the line and short throws that should keep the offense on schedule add little or subtract value. That makes the offense dependent on longer developing plays behind a line that lets him get pressured often, with a 28.4% pressure rate that ranks 33rd of 37. This looks more like a design and line problem than a flaw in him, but it raises the floor risk when downfield throws are covered.

trend.note: His first two games combined strong EPA with double-digit CPOE, and his accuracy has slid since. The last three games produced one strong outing against the league's worst defense and two below-expected passing days. Yardage has held steady at around 300 a game because the volume has not changed.

nextGame.headline: Stingy Tampa coverage, but no pass rush and a depleted secondary
nextGame.body:
Tampa Bay is a hard defense on paper: fourth in EPA, sixth against the pass, seventh on short throws, and sixth in limiting explosive passes. It has held lead receivers well under their averages. The weakness is up front, where it ranks 26th in hit rate and 22nd in sack rate. That suits a passer who takes a lot of pressure and needs time for routes at 10 to 19 yards. Deep throws, at 15th, are the softest area of its pass defense.

Availability favors Carolina. Safety Antoine Winfield Jr. (97% of snaps) and corner Benjamin Morrison are out, which weakens the deep middle where Young has been best. Freeling, the left tackle who missed Week 6, carries a return date of this game; having him back would improve the protection that slipped in Philadelphia. On the other side, Baker Mayfield is listed out with a dislocated thumb, though Todd Bowles said he is supposed to practice. Without Mayfield, Tampa's 31st-ranked passing offense could hand Carolina an early lead, which may cut Young's volume more than the defense limits his efficiency.

keyMatchups.title: McMillan into Tampa's WR1 lockdown
keyMatchups.body: Tampa has held opposing top receivers further below their averages than any defense, while second receivers have scored the most over their averages. If McMillan is shadowed, Coker becomes the volume outlet, and his 0.388 EPA per target is not much below McMillan's. Young's spread is likely to shift toward the No. 2.

keyMatchups.title: Weak rush versus a pressured QB
keyMatchups.body: Tampa rarely hits or sacks quarterbacks, which should give Young cleaner pockets than usual. His downfield game depends on time to throw, at 2.92 seconds, so a quiet rush is the best path to his intermediate strengths.

keyMatchups.title: Short-area squeeze, deep opening
keyMatchups.body: Tampa is stingy on short throws, which is already Young's weakest zone. Its deep EPA allowed is middling, and Winfield's absence makes the deep area softer still.

nextGame.watch: Whether his accuracy on throws over the middle at 10 to 19 yards returns with Winfield out, or whether the CPOE slide of the last three weeks continues against a top-six pass defense.

restOfSeason.body:
The pass-heavy design and his snap share make him a dependable volume producer, and the improvements in sack avoidance and bad throws look like real development rather than noise. What should come down is the downfield efficiency built on small samples, especially the +12 deep CPOE, along with the touchdown rate and the 1% interception rate. I expect roughly 250-295 passing yards a game with EPA per dropback settling between 0.05 and 0.14. That is still clearly better than any of his first three seasons, but closer to good starter than top-ten.

The ceiling depends on the protection and the quick game. If the short throws start adding value and Freeling stays healthy, he can hold most of this level. If the line keeps letting him get pressured and third downs stay long, expect more games like Cleveland's.
swingFactors: Monroe Freeling's health at left tackle
Whether deep and intermediate accuracy holds on a bigger sample
Game scripts with leads reducing pass volume

confidence.note: Five games that break sharply from three seasons of career norms, with efficiency already easing.
